findings.reason: §2's search must begin from the delta path, because the cheapest repair may be to route the first review through the same delta machinery rather than to teach a new helper three-dot ranges.
findings.text: an incremental run review already exists and covers exactly the commits a run gained since the head its last review read (`goal` naming `delta["paths"]`, `scope`, `delta_base`, `review_tier = LIGHT` at :1055-:1058), fed by `review_head_move` and the two-dot `_changed_paths_between` at `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:937`, with `git merge-base` already on both read allowlists (`reckon/worker_git_shim.py:120`, `reckon/shadow_reads.py:42`); the plan cites none of it and so proposes a second notion of "a run's changes" beside an existing one

findings.reason: §2's premise that the review was "sized on" the base..head range is unverified by the named code, and a repair that only narrows the range may leave the 670392-token estimate untouched; §2 must name routing.py as the estimate's owner and record which input term produced the figure before any range change is proposed.
findings.text: the plan names this line as where "the context-fit estimate whose refusal text is built", but it only renders routing's detail (`_rendered_context_detail`, :584); the estimate is built in `reckon/crew/routing.py:3262` (`_context_file_inputs`) and summed at :3580-:3595, and it reads no git range at all — its terms are the standing instruction chain (`:3159`), the node's declared write paths, and paths declared as inputs or merely mentioned in the node's `goal`/`done_when` prose

findings.reason: §2's done-when says it "names every place that takes the range from the record's base_sha to the head", so the census must be larger than the three files the plan cites, and the repair must extend `clones.changed_paths` (with the merge base taken once, and `review.py`'s carried pair kept as the review's identity) rather than add a thirteenth range reader.
findings.text: twelve sites already compute a range from the record's `base_sha` to a head or tip, and the plan names no owner to extend for the one it proposes: `reckon/clones.py:629` (`changed_paths(tree, base_sha, tip)`, the two-dot helper), `reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py:658` (shadow brief, `git -C {worktree} diff {base}`), `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:937` `_changed_paths_between` with callers at :971, :1039, :1091, `reckon/crew/review.py:402` (`REVIEWED_BASE_KEY`) read at :2585 and :3008, `reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py:271`, :523, :550, :619, :976, `reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:596`, `reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py:980`, `reckon/crew/landing_measure.py:534` and :610, `reckon/crew/routing.py:1514`, `reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:2501`, and the one site that already excludes the integration branch, `reckon/crew/node.py:1537` (`git rev-list HEAD ^integration_ref ^base_sha`)

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan adds no module; its single implementable section is an investigation, so no new interface is proposed for a depth claim, and the repair section it must write is where that claim will be judged.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — twelve modules already take a range from the record's `base_sha` to the head, owned by `reckon/clones.py:629` (`changed_paths`) and `reckon/crew/review.py:402` (`REVIEWED_BASE_KEY`), and the plan names neither owner.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 2361, cli_options 465, mcp_views 15, refusal_families 23; the plan's two sections add nothing to any of these families, and the context refusal it is about reuses the existing `D08` family rather than declaring a new one.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan proposes a merge-base range for a review without citing the incremental review already in the tree (`_review_dispatch_fields(delta=…)` and `review_head_move`), nor `clones.changed_paths`, nor the one existing range that already excludes the integration branch (`node.py:1537`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan adds no layer over existing machinery; the extension-not-fork requirement therefore lands on the repair section §2 must write, and is carried below as the duplicate-owner finding's ask.
